summary.problem:
Streamlit Crashing with Error: `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

**UPDATE**: I believe the culprit is a bug in the `@st.cache_resource` logic and/or the way streamlit handles db connections that try to persist (had same issues using `session_state`). See my follow-up message below. 

My initial issue:

Unfortunately I have a fairly complicated app. My streamlit application is crashing and I'm not sure why. The error seems somewhat ominous, but there's really not much information that helps me figure out what's going on, which is why I've made this issue. 

I've seen this error on rare occasion when building my complex application. Normally, this happens after I update the file and hit 'rerun', so I just chalk it up to: something happens when I hot-reload a new version of the file that breaks things. Nothing I'm concerned about since I don't expect to do this in production.

However, after adding a normal [selectbox](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/widgets/st.selectbox), streamlit intermittently crashes when I use [this](https://github.com/hoggatt/st-combobox) simple custom component that gives me the ability to define my own auto complete function. I don't actually think it's related to the combobox itself, it's just that when the combobox is auto-completing, it's rerunning a lot. This was working before I added a normal `st.textbox`, but now it's completely broken. However, the fact that I saw it very infrequently before indicates to me it's probably not directly related to the selectbox. 


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# THIS IS PSEUDO-CODE #

search_input = st.text_input()

...
many conditional statements doing something with the search input including setting st.experimental_set_query_params at one point
also queries the database using a cached_resource mysql connector (see below)
...

value = st.selectbox(items based on search_input)

# allow selecting something using a combobox (st-combobox) with autocomplete
def search_files(searchterm):
  refine search based (in part) on value
selected_value = st_combobox(search_files, ...)

# this method is cached
file = get_file(selected_value)

...
setting up controls for the plot based on the file loaded

summary.problem:
Preserve Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position in st.dataframe

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Today, when a page is refreshed / app gets rerun / data for dataframe changes, the dataframe completely refreshes. Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position are lost. 

This makes it hard to work with data within the dataframe and change it by means of a Master Detail View for example.

Idea is: Preserve Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position in st.dataframe when data is reloaded / the page is rerun.


### Why?

Scenario: A Master Detail View: The dataframe is part of the Master View within the page, and the Detail View enables the user to edit certain fields (not all are visible in the dataframe). After changing some data, the dataframe is reloaded and selection, sorting, scrolling position are lost.

### How?

The selection currently is set in the session, but it is not considered when the page is reloaded. 

Sorting is not part of the state.

Scrolling position is preserved for st.container today, but not for st.dataframe.

Solution idea:
- Store selection and sorting in session_state and use this information when the page is rerun and the dataframe is rendered.
- Use the implementation of st.container to preserve scrolling position.

### Additional Context


This issue is related to, however they only cover parts of this idea. 

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8851
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10128

### Checklist

- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In attempt to create a dynamic filter in a dialog box, I stumbled on the fact updating a session_state variable via a custom component is not possible. 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
Something as simple as this code does not execute:

if "test_text" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["test_text"] = None 

@st.experimental_dialog(title="Test", width="small")
def test_dialog():

    import streamlit_antd_components as sac

    def onChangeTest():

        st.session_state["test_text"] = st.session_state["testing123"] 
    

    sac.chip(
        items=[
            sac.ChipItem(label='apple'),
            sac.ChipItem(label='google'),
            sac.ChipItem(label='github', icon='github'),
            sac.ChipItem(label='twitter', icon='twitter'),
        ], label='label', index=0, align='center', radius='md', multiple=False, key="testing123", on_change=onChangeTest
    )
    st.write(st.session_state["test_text"])

st.button("Test", key="test_btn")

if st.session_state["test_btn"]:
    test_dialog()


```

But it works with native widgets:
```
if "test_text" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["test_text"] = None 

@st.experimental_dialog(title="Test", width="small")
def test_dialog():

    import streamlit_antd_components as sac

    def onChangeTest():

       st.session_state["test_text"] = st.session_state["testing123"] 
    
       st.radio("dummy label", ["one", "two", "three", "four"], key="testing123",on_change=onChangeTest )

   
       st.write(st.session_state["test_text"])


st.button("Test", key="test_btn")

if st.session_state["test_btn"]:
    test_dialog()

```
```

summary.problem:
st.slider silently mis-represents dates outside the frontend number range

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.slider` accepts `date`/`datetime` bounds that the frontend cannot represent exactly, and silently snaps them to a different instant instead of reporting the problem. The `int` and `float` paths already validate and raise a helpful `StreamlitAPIException`; the timelike path does not.

Timelike values are serialized as microseconds since the epoch and held in a JavaScript number on the frontend, so only about **1684-07-28 to 2255-06-05** round-trips exactly. Outside that, precision is lost.

`lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/slider.py` acknowledges the gap:

```python
elif all_timelikes:
    # No validation yet. TODO: check between 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31
    pass
```

Worth noting the TODO's own target range is wrong — most of `0001`–`9999` is not representable, so validating to those limits would not have fixed it.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import datetime as dt
import streamlit as st

# Silently accepted, but min_value cannot be represented exactly:
st.slider("historical", min_value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(1700, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1))

# Also silently accepted, both bounds unrepresentable:
st.slider("projection", min_value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(2400, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1))

# Raises a bare OverflowError instead of a StreamlitAPIException:
st.slider("ancient", value=dt.date(1, 1, 1))
```

### Actual Behavior

Inspecting the serialized proto shows the bounds exceeding JavaScript's `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` with no error raised:

```
in-range 1900..2000      -> NO ERROR. min=-2208988800000000 max=946684800000000  JS-unsafe: none
historical 1600..1700    -> NO ERROR. min=-11676096000000000                      JS-unsafe: ['min']
far future 2300..2400    -> NO ERROR. min=10413792000000000 max=13569465600000000 JS-unsafe: ['min', 'max']
min date 0001..0002      -> OverflowError: date value out of range
```

Two distinct problems:

1. **Moderately out-of-range values are accepted and lose precision.** Years like 1600 or 2300 are ordinary in historical datasets and long-range projections, so this is not just an exotic edge case.
2. **E

slider(min=10, max=1, value=1)   -> RAISED: Slider `min_value` must be less than the `max_value`.
                                            The values were 1 and 1.

summary.problem:
st.slider silently mis-represents dates outside the frontend number range

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.slider` accepts `date`/`datetime` bounds that the frontend cannot represent exactly, and silently snaps them to a different instant instead of reporting the problem. The `int` and `float` paths already validate and raise a helpful `StreamlitAPIException`; the timelike path does not.

Timelike values are serialized as microseconds since the epoch and held in a JavaScript number on the frontend, so only about **1684-07-28 to 2255-06-05** round-trips exactly. Outside that, precision is lost.

`lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/slider.py` acknowledges the gap:

```python
elif all_timelikes:
    # No validation yet. TODO: check between 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31
    pass
```

Worth noting the TODO's own target range is wrong — most of `0001`–`9999` is not representable, so validating to those limits would not have fixed it.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import datetime as dt
import streamlit as st

# Silently accepted, but min_value cannot be represented exactly:
st.slider("historical", min_value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(1700, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1))

# Also silently accepted, both bounds unrepresentable:
st.slider("projection", min_value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(2400, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1))

# Raises a bare OverflowError instead of a StreamlitAPIException:
st.slider("ancient", value=dt.date(1, 1, 1))
```

### Actual Behavior

Inspecting the serialized proto shows the bounds exceeding JavaScript's `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` with no error raised:

```
in-range 1900..2000      -> NO ERROR. min=-2208988800000000 max=946684800000000  JS-unsafe: none
historical 1600..1700    -> NO ERROR. min=-11676096000000000                      JS-unsafe: ['min']
far future 2300..2400    -> NO ERROR. min=10413792000000000 max=13569465600000000 JS-unsafe: ['min', 'max']
min date 0001..0002      -> OverflowError: date value out of range
```

Two distinct problems:

1. **Moderately out-of-range values are accepted and lose precision.** Years like 1600 or 2300 are ordinary in historical datasets and long-range projections, so this is not just an exotic edge case.
2. **E

summary.problem:
Add a button group widget with trigger (click) mode

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Provide a button group that supports **trigger (click) mode** instead of selection mode — i.e. a horizontal group of buttons that returns the clicked value once (like `st.button`) and clears after the rerun, rather than persisting a selection. This can either be a new `st.button_group` command or an extension of the existing `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`.

### Why?

It's currently a bit complicated to build things like quick selections / quick replies for chat UIs (a major need for LLM-powered apps), button toolbars, dialog action rows (Confirm / Cancel / Clear), or clickable example grids. Today you have to combine many individual `st.button`s across `st.columns`, which is a lot of boilerplate and looks messy because wrapping depends on each button's label length.

### How?

Two main options:

**Option 1 — Extend `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` with a trigger mode:**

```python
st.pills(..., selection_mode="single" | "multi" | "trigger")
```

In `trigger` mode the widget doesn't keep state: it returns the clicked value and clears it after the rerun (like a button), returning `None` otherwise. `default` wouldn't be allowed in this mode.

**Option 2 — Add a dedicated `st.button_group` command (preferred):**

```python
st.button_group(
    options,
    *,
    format_func=None,
    key=None,
    on_click=None,
    args=None,
    kwargs=None,
    disabled=False,
    type="default" | "rounded",
    wrap=True,
)
```

Behaves like `st.pills` but tailored for triggers: no top label/help (not needed for quick selections), `on_click` instead of `on_change` (aligns with `st.button`), a `type` option for a rounded pill-like look, and a `wrap` option. Keeping triggers in a separate command avoids overloading the selection API (e.g. `selection_mode="trigger"` reads oddly, `default` becomes incompatible, and typing gets awkward).

### Additional Context

- Related: #8318 (quick replies/suggestions for chat responses) — one of the primary motivating use cases.
- Other use cases: button toolbars, dialog action rows, and clickable example grids.

summary.problem:
Add a button group widget with trigger (click) mode

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Provide a button group that supports **trigger (click) mode** instead of selection mode — i.e. a horizontal group of buttons that returns the clicked value once (like `st.button`) and clears after the rerun, rather than persisting a selection. This can either be a new `st.button_group` command or an extension of the existing `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`.

### Why?

It's currently a bit complicated to build things like quick selections / quick replies for chat UIs (a major need for LLM-powered apps), button toolbars, dialog action rows (Confirm / Cancel / Clear), or clickable example grids. Today you have to combine many individual `st.button`s across `st.columns`, which is a lot of boilerplate and looks messy because wrapping depends on each button's label length.

### How?

Two main options:

**Option 1 — Extend `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` with a trigger mode:**

```python
st.pills(..., selection_mode="single" | "multi" | "trigger")
```

In `trigger` mode the widget doesn't keep state: it returns the clicked value and clears it after the rerun (like a button), returning `None` otherwise. `default` wouldn't be allowed in this mode.

**Option 2 — Add a dedicated `st.button_group` command (preferred):**

```python
st.button_group(
    options,
    *,
    format_func=None,
    key=None,
    on_click=None,
    args=None,
    kwargs=None,
    disabled=False,
    type="default" | "rounded",
    wrap=True,
)
```

Behaves like `st.pills` but tailored for triggers: no top label/help (not needed for quick selections), `on_click` instead of `on_change` (aligns with `st.button`), a `type` option for a rounded pill-like look, and a `wrap` option. Keeping triggers in a separate command avoids overloading the selection API (e.g. `selection_mode="trigger"` reads oddly, `default` becomes incompatible, and typing gets awkward).

### Additional Context

- Related: #8318 (quick replies/suggestions for chat responses) — one of the primary motivating use cases.
- Other use cases: button toolbars, dialog action rows, and clickable example grids.

summary.problem:
Add a `type="cards"` variant to `st.radio` for a card/bordered design

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.radio` with a `"cards"` variant that renders each option as a bordered, selectable card (with the selected card highlighted) instead of the default radio-button list. Same widget behavior — only the visual style changes. See [Tremor's Radio Card Group](https://www.tremor.so/docs/inputs/radio-card-group) for the look.

### Why?

Card-style single-select is a very common, more prominent and touch-friendly pattern for choosing between a few richer options (e.g. plans, payment methods, layouts, modes). Today users approximate it with columns + bordered containers + buttons/`st.radio` and a lot of manual state/CSS work. A built-in `"cards"` variant makes this polished pattern a one-liner.

### How?

Add a `type` parameter (default preserves today's look):

```python
choice = st.radio(
    "Choose a plan",
    ["Starter", "Pro", "Enterprise"],
    captions=[
        "For individuals getting started",
        "For growing teams",
        "Advanced controls & support",
    ],
    type="cards",
)
```

- `type="default"` — current radio-button list.
- `type="cards"` — render each option as a bordered card; the selected option is visually highlighted.
- Keep existing params working (`captions`, `horizontal`, `format_func`, `index=None`, etc.). Captions map naturally to a description line inside each card.

**Alternative solution — a `border: bool` parameter:** Instead of a `type` enum, just add `st.radio(..., border=True)` that wraps each option in a bordered card. This mirrors the `border` parameter on `st.container` and keeps the API minimal. Downside: it's less extensible than a `type` enum if we later want more visual variants (e.g. `"pills"`), and it's a boolean rather than a named style.

### Additional Context

- Reference designs:
  - [Tremor — Radio Card Group](https://www.tremor.so/docs/inputs/radio-card-group)
  - [Tailwind Plus — Radio Groups (card designs)](https://tailwindcss.com/plus/ui-blocks/application-ui/forms/radio-groups)
  - [streamlit-extras — Card Selector](https://extras.streamlit.app/?extra=%F0%9F%83%8F+Card+Selector) (existing community implementation)
- Related: #2325 (`st.radio` with sections), #7184 (stretch horizontal radio), #119

summary.problem:
When using the unique method of pandas, the st.cache_data method is invalid  in some cases.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When I take the result of pandas' unique method as the parameter of the cache_data function, the function will always be triggered again. In addition, it is puzzling that the cache is valid when the data type of pd.Series is numeric or each row is only a single letter, for example, df ['str ']=['a', 'a', 'b', 'c']. But the cache is invalid when df ['str ']=['be', 'a', 'be', 'c'].

### Reproducible Code Example

[[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-6182)

```Python
import numpy as np
import streamlit as st
import time
import pandas as pd

'''
streamlit == 1.18.1
pandas == 1.5.0
'''

@st.cache_data()
def get_data():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"num":[112,112,2,3],"str":['be','a','be','c']})
    return df

@st.cache_data()
def show_data(data):
    time.sleep(1)
    return data

df = get_data()
data = df['str'].unique()

index_daily_data = show_data(data)
st.dataframe(index_daily_data)
st.button("rerun")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1.Use streamlit to run the above program.
2.You will see that the show_data function will be called repeatedly.
3.Remove the unique function or modify the df = pd.DataFrame({"num":[112,112,2,3],"str":['b','a','b','c']}) or  modify data = df['num'].unique(), the cache will take effect normally.

```

Page layout is not "centered" by default in multipage apps

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Page layout is not "centered" by default in multipage apps, as would be expected by the default value in [st.set_page_config](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/utilities/st.set_page_config#stset_page_config). 

Instead, it inherits the layout from the previously visited page.

I would call it a bug, but could also hear that this is expected because no explicit call to st.set_page_config was made... 

Example:
[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
#streamlit_app.py
import streamlit as st

st.write(st.__version__)
st.title("Hello world")
```

```
#pages/one.py
import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(layout="wide")
st.title("Wide layout")
```

```
#pages/two.py
import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(layout="centered")
st.title("Centered layout")
```
```


### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

The `streamlit_app` page should have its layout = `"centered"`, as is meant to be the default for `st.set_page_config()`.

### Current Behavior

The `streamlit_app` page inherits its layout from the previously visited page

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.19.0
- Python version: 
- Operating System: Mac OSX
- Browser: Chrome
- Virtual environment: None

### Summary

**UPDATE**: I believe the culprit is a bug in the `@st.cache_resource` logic and/or the way streamlit handles db connections that try to persist (had same issues using `session_state`). See my follow-up message below. 

My initial issue:

Unfortunately I have a fairly complicated app. My streamlit application is crashing and I'm not sure why. The error seems somewhat ominous, but there's really not much information that helps me figure out what's going on, which is why I've made this issue. 

I've seen this error on rare occasion when building my complex application. Normally, this happens after I update the file and hit 'rerun', so I just chalk it up to: something happens when I hot-reload a new version of the file that breaks things. Nothing I'm concerned about since I don't expect to do this in production.

However, after adding a normal [selectbox](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/widgets/st.selectbox), streamlit intermittently crashes when I use [this](https://github.com/hoggatt/st-combobox) simple custom component that gives me the ability to define my own auto complete function. I don't actually think it's related to the combobox itself, it's just that when the combobox is auto-completing, it's rerunning a lot. This was working before I added a normal `st.textbox`, but now it's completely broken. However, the fact that I saw it very infrequently before indicates to me it's probably not directly related to the selectbox. 


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# THIS IS PSEUDO-CODE #

search_input = st.text_input()

...
many conditional statements doing something with the search input including setting st.experimental_set_query_params at one point
also queries the database using a cached_resource mysql connector (see below)
...

# allow selecting something using a combobox (st-combobox) with autocomplete

  refine search based (in part) on value

# this method is cached
file = get_file(selected_value)

...
setting up controls for the plot based on the file loaded

summary.problem:
Preserve Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position in st.dataframe

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Today, when a page is refreshed / app gets rerun / data for dataframe changes, the dataframe completely refreshes. Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position are lost. 

This makes it hard to work with data within the dataframe and change it by means of a Master Detail View for example.

Idea is: Preserve Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position in st.dataframe when data is reloaded / the page is rerun.


### Why?

Scenario: A Master Detail View: The dataframe is part of the Master View within the page, and the Detail View enables the user to edit certain fields (not all are visible in the dataframe). After changing some data, the dataframe is reloaded and selection, sorting, scrolling position are lost.

### How?

The selection currently is set in the session, but it is not considered when the page is reloaded. 

Sorting is not part of the state.

Scrolling position is preserved for st.container today, but not for st.dataframe.

Solution idea:
- Store selection and sorting in session_state and use this information when the page is rerun and the dataframe is rendered.
- Use the implementation of st.container to preserve scrolling position.

### Additional Context


This issue is related to, however they only cover parts of this idea. 

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8851
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10128

### Summary

In attempt to create a dynamic filter in a dialog box, I stumbled on the fact updating a session_state variable via a custom component is not possible. 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
Something as simple as this code does not execute:

if "test_text" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["test_text"] = None 

@st.experimental_dialog(title="Test", width="small")
def test_dialog():

    import streamlit_antd_components as sac

    def onChangeTest():

        st.session_state["test_text"] = st.session_state["testing123"] 
    

    sac.chip(
        items=[
            sac.ChipItem(label='apple'),
            sac.ChipItem(label='google'),
            sac.ChipItem(label='github', icon='github'),
            sac.ChipItem(label='twitter', icon='twitter'),
        ], label='label', index=0, align='center', radius='md', multiple=False, key="testing123", on_change=onChangeTest
    )
    st.write(st.session_state["test_text"])

st.button("Test", key="test_btn")

if st.session_state["test_btn"]:
    test_dialog()


```

But it works with native widgets:
```
if "test_text" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["test_text"] = None 

@st.experimental_dialog(title="Test", width="small")
def test_dialog():

    import streamlit_antd_components as sac

       st.session_state["test_text"] = st.session_state["testing123"]

st.button("Test", key="test_btn")

summary.problem:
Add a button group widget with trigger (click) mode

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Provide a button group that supports **trigger (click) mode** instead of selection mode — i.e. a horizontal group of buttons that returns the clicked value once (like `st.button`) and clears after the rerun, rather than persisting a selection. This can either be a new `st.button_group` command or an extension of the existing `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`.

### Why?

It's currently a bit complicated to build things like quick selections / quick replies for chat UIs (a major need for LLM-powered apps), button toolbars, dialog action rows (Confirm / Cancel / Clear), or clickable example grids. Today you have to combine many individual `st.button`s across `st.columns`, which is a lot of boilerplate and looks messy because wrapping depends on each button's label length.

### How?

Two main options:

**Option 1 — Extend `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` with a trigger mode:**

```python
st.pills(..., selection_mode="single" | "multi" | "trigger")
```

In `trigger` mode the widget doesn't keep state: it returns the clicked value and clears it after the rerun (like a button), returning `None` otherwise. `default` wouldn't be allowed in this mode.

**Option 2 — Add a dedicated `st.button_group` command (preferred):**

```python
st.button_group(
    options,
    *,
    format_func=None,
    key=None,
    on_click=None,
    args=None,
    kwargs=None,
    disabled=False,
    type="default" | "rounded",
    wrap=True,
)
```

Behaves like `st.pills` but tailored for triggers: no top label/help (not needed for quick selections), `on_click` instead of `on_change` (aligns with `st.button`), a `type` option for a rounded pill-like look, and a `wrap` option. Keeping triggers in a separate command avoids overloading the selection API (e.g. `selection_mode="trigger"` reads oddly, `default` becomes incompatible, and typing gets awkward).

### Additional Context

- Related: #8318 (quick replies/suggestions for chat responses) — one of the primary motivating use cases.
- Other use cases: button toolbars, dialog action rows, and clickable example grids.

summary.problem:
Add a button group widget with trigger (click) mode

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Provide a button group that supports **trigger (click) mode** instead of selection mode — i.e. a horizontal group of buttons that returns the clicked value once (like `st.button`) and clears after the rerun, rather than persisting a selection. This can either be a new `st.button_group` command or an extension of the existing `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`.

### Why?

It's currently a bit complicated to build things like quick selections / quick replies for chat UIs (a major need for LLM-powered apps), button toolbars, dialog action rows (Confirm / Cancel / Clear), or clickable example grids. Today you have to combine many individual `st.button`s across `st.columns`, which is a lot of boilerplate and looks messy because wrapping depends on each button's label length.

### How?

Two main options:

**Option 1 — Extend `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` with a trigger mode:**

```python
st.pills(..., selection_mode="single" | "multi" | "trigger")
```

In `trigger` mode the widget doesn't keep state: it returns the clicked value and clears it after the rerun (like a button), returning `None` otherwise. `default` wouldn't be allowed in this mode.

**Option 2 — Add a dedicated `st.button_group` command (preferred):**

```python
st.button_group(
    options,
    *,
    format_func=None,
    key=None,
    on_click=None,
    args=None,
    kwargs=None,
    disabled=False,
    type="default" | "rounded",
    wrap=True,
)
```

Behaves like `st.pills` but tailored for triggers: no top label/help (not needed for quick selections), `on_click` instead of `on_change` (aligns with `st.button`), a `type` option for a rounded pill-like look, and a `wrap` option. Keeping triggers in a separate command avoids overloading the selection API (e.g. `selection_mode="trigger"` reads oddly, `default` becomes incompatible, and typing gets awkward).

### Additional Context

- Related: #8318 (quick replies/suggestions for chat responses) — one of the primary motivating use cases.
- Other use cases: button toolbars, dialog action rows, and clickable example grids.

summary.problem:
Add a `type="cards"` variant to `st.radio` for a card/bordered design

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.radio` with a `"cards"` variant that renders each option as a bordered, selectable card (with the selected card highlighted) instead of the default radio-button list. Same widget behavior — only the visual style changes. See [Tremor's Radio Card Group](https://www.tremor.so/docs/inputs/radio-card-group) for the look.

### Why?

Card-style single-select is a very common, more prominent and touch-friendly pattern for choosing between a few richer options (e.g. plans, payment methods, layouts, modes). Today users approximate it with columns + bordered containers + buttons/`st.radio` and a lot of manual state/CSS work. A built-in `"cards"` variant makes this polished pattern a one-liner.

### How?

Add a `type` parameter (default preserves today's look):

```python
choice = st.radio(
    "Choose a plan",
    ["Starter", "Pro", "Enterprise"],
    captions=[
        "For individuals getting started",
        "For growing teams",
        "Advanced controls & support",
    ],
    type="cards",
)
```

- `type="default"` — current radio-button list.
- `type="cards"` — render each option as a bordered card; the selected option is visually highlighted.
- Keep existing params working (`captions`, `horizontal`, `format_func`, `index=None`, etc.). Captions map naturally to a description line inside each card.

**Alternative solution — a `border: bool` parameter:** Instead of a `type` enum, just add `st.radio(..., border=True)` that wraps each option in a bordered card. This mirrors the `border` parameter on `st.container` and keeps the API minimal. Downside: it's less extensible than a `type` enum if we later want more visual variants (e.g. `"pills"`), and it's a boolean rather than a named style.

### Additional Context

- Reference designs:
  - [Tremor — Radio Card Group](https://www.tremor.so/docs/inputs/radio-card-group)
  - [Tailwind Plus — Radio Groups (card designs)](https://tailwindcss.com/plus/ui-blocks/application-ui/forms/radio-groups)
  - [streamlit-extras — Card Selector](https://extras.streamlit.app/?extra=%F0%9F%83%8F+Card+Selector) (existing community implementation)
- Related: #2325 (`st.radio` with sections), #7184 (stretch horizontal radio), #119

محدودیت: اسناد رسمی نشان می‌دهد که داده‌های فایل آپلود شده با `st.file_uploader` در حافظه RAM (بافر BytesIO) ذخیره می‌شوند و با برخی تعاملات مانند جایگزینی فایل یا پاک کردن آن یا بسته شدن تب مرورگر پاک می‌شوند. این می‌تواند موجب شود که اقدام به خواندن فایل پس از بسته شدن آن باعث خطای I/O روی فایل بسته شود. از آنجا که کاربر به نسخه 0.70.0 اشاره دارد که قدیمی است و گزارش‌هایی از مشکلات مشابه در این زمینه وجود دارد، لازم است داده‌های دقیق‌تری درباره کد و رفتاری که قبل و بعد از انتخاب شکل می‌گیرد، بدست آوریم تا تشخیص دقیق‌تری انجام شود.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: خطا احتمالاً به دلیل بسته شدن غیرمنتظره فایل آپلود شده در جریان اجرای دوباره اپ است.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: احتمال دارد فایل آپلود شده در حافظه موقت (RAM) نگهداری می‌شود و به محض بارگذاری دوباره یا تغییر داده‌ها بسته شود.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: ممکن است عملکرد `file_uploader` با نسخه Streamlit فعلی که کاربر استفاده می‌کند، محدودیت‌هایی در حفظ فایل باز پس از تعاملات وجود داشته باشد.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.

summary.problem:
st.sidebar.beta_expander does not read a st.sidebar.file_uploader

### Summary

In the main page, we can have a `file_uploader` within a `beta_expander`, however this does not seem to work as soon as it is put in the `sidebar`.

### Steps to reproduce

Try to run this code snippet:

```
with st.sidebar.beta_expander("Input file", expanded=True):
    input_file = st.sidebar.file_uploader(
        "Input your file", type=[".csv"]
    )
```
you will see that the `file_uploader` is outside of the `beta_expander` box, and that the `beta_expander` box is empty.
Instead, when running on the main page and not on the sidebar, everythng works fine:
```
with st.beta_expander("Input file", expanded=True):
    input_file = st.file_uploader(
        "Input your file", type=[".csv"]
    )
```

It is not a regression to my knowledge, but I have only started to use the `beta_expander` recently - so I may be wrong. 

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.79.0
- Python version: 3.7.6
- Using Conda

retrieved.section: Where does st.file_uploader store uploaded files and when do they get deleted?

output.response:
پاسخ پیشنهادی: آیا در مستندات رسمی Streamlit یا ورژن 1.49.0 و بالاتر پارامتری برای فعال کردن بازخورد بصری هنگام هاور روی ناحیه بارگذاری فایل وجود دارد؟ آیا امکان افزودن و ویرایش CSS سفارشی برای این ویجت فراهم شده است؟

شاهد مستند: متن رسمی؛ سازگاری نسخه باید بررسی شود.

بخش منبع:

```text
Where does st.file_uploader store uploaded files and when do they get deleted?
```

نسخهٔ منبع:

```text
695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd
```

متن شاهد:

```text
When you upload a file using [`st.file_uploader`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader), the data are copied to the Streamlit backend via the browser, and contained in a BytesIO buffer in Python memory (i.e. RAM, not disk). The data will persist in RAM until the Streamlit app re-runs from top-to-bottom, which is on each widget interaction. If you need to save the data that was uploaded between runs, then you can [cache](/develop/concepts/architecture/caching) it so that Streamlit persists it across re-runs.
```

```

بخش منبع:

```text
file_uploader (line 252)
```

نسخهٔ منبع:

```text
1.49.0
```

متن شاهد:

```text
- ``False`` (default): The user can only submit one file at a time.
    - ``True``: The user can upload multiple files at the same time.
    - ``"directory"``: The user can select a directory to upload all
      files in the directory and its subdirectories. If ``type`` is
      set, only files matching those type(s) will be uploaded.
```

نشانی منبع:

```text
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/1.49.0/lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/file_uploader.py
```

محدودیت: با توجه به بررسی مستندات `st.file_uploader` و توضیحاتی درباره نحوه ذخیره سازی فایل‌ها و پارامترهای ورودی ویجت، هیچ ادعایی مبنی بر وجود قابلیت بازخورد بصری دقیقاً هنگام هاور روی ناحیه بارگذاری فایل مشاهده نشده است. بنابراین نیاز به انجام پرسش برای مشخص کردن امکان چنین ویژگی یا راه حل جایگزین برای کاربر وجود دارد.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: ممکن است که UI موجود برای `st.file_uploader` قابلیت نمایش بازخورد بصری در هنگام هاور روی ناحیه کشیدن فایل را ندارد.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: ممکن است که گزینه ای مانند `highlight_on_hover` در پارامترهای `st.file_uploader` فعلاً در دسترس نباشد.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: ممکن است که نیاز به افزودن چنین قابلیتی با تغییرات در رابط کاربری یا CSS سفارشی وجود داشته باشد.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.

### Summary

When I take the result of pandas' unique method as the parameter of the cache_data function, the function will always be triggered again. [[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-6182)

import numpy as np
import streamlit as st
import time
import pandas as pd

streamlit == 1.18.1
pandas == 1.5.0
'''

@st.cache_data()
def get_data():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"num":[112,112,2,3],"str":['be','a','be','c']})
    return df

@st.cache_data()
def show_data(data):
    time.sleep(1)
    return data

df = get_data()
data = df['str'].unique()

index_daily_data = show_data(data)
st.dataframe(index_daily_data)
st.button("rerun")
```

sources.quote:
When using ``st.navigation``, your entrypoint file (the file passed to
``streamlit run``) acts like a router or frame of common elements around
each of your pages. Streamlit executes the entrypoint file with every app
rerun. To execute the current page, you must call the ``.run()`` method on
the ``StreamlitPage`` object returned by ``st.navigation``.

The primary way users navigate between pages is through the navigation widget. Both methods for defining multipage apps include a default navigation menu that appears in the sidebar. When a user clicks this navigation widget, the app reruns and loads the selected page. Optionally, you can hide the default navigation UI and build your own with [`st.page_link`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.page_link). For more information, see [Build a custom navigation menu with `st.page_link`](/develop/tutorials/multipage/st.page_link-nav).

`st.Page` lets you define a page. The first and only required argument defines your page source, which can be a Python file or function. When using Python files, your pages may be in a subdirectory (or superdirectory). The path to your page file must always be relative to the entrypoint file. Once you create your page objects, pass them to `st.navigation` to register them as pages in your app.
